clue.text: Poorly Alec OK facing doctor somewhere in northern Italy

indicators.note: facing says the first part sits up against the second, in front of it
something poorly is in bad shape, so the letters of Alec and OK are put out of order

parts.note: MO is a medical officer, a standard abbreviation for a doctor

explanation.surface: An unwell man called Alec, now fine, is seeing a doctor while on holiday in Italy.
explanation.definitionFit: Lake Como is a large Alpine lake in Lombardy, in the north of Italy.

clue.text: Some fully restore old musical instrument

indicators.note: Some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A restorer bringing an antique instrument back to full condition.
explanation.definitionFit: The lyre is a small harp-like stringed instrument from ancient Greece.

clue.text: Child, glowing, lifted church somewhere in West Midlands

parts.note: a kid is a child

indicators.note: in a down clue lifting a word turns it upside down, so it reads backwards

parts.note: red as in red-hot, glowing with heat
a minster is a large church, such as York Minster

explanation.surface: A shining child holds up a church in the Midlands.
explanation.definitionFit: Kidderminster is a town in Worcestershire, a county in the West Midlands region of England, famous for carpets.

clue.text: Private Honda convertible within easy reach

parts.note: closet as an adjective means secret or private, as in a closet fan

indicators.note: convertible means able to be changed, so the letters of Honda are turned into another order

explanation.surface: A soldier's open-topped Japanese car is parked nearby.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Private' looks like a soldier and 'convertible' like a car; they are an adjective and an anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Close to hand is an idiom meaning nearby and readily available.

clue.text: Large fish right and left in sea

indicators.note: in places the two letters within the word for the sea

parts.note: the main is a poetic word for the open sea

explanation.surface: A big fish swimming this way and that in the ocean.
explanation.definitionFit: The marlin is a large ocean game fish with a long spear-like snout.

clue.text: Tip left among snooker equipment

indicators.note: among puts one letter in the middle of the other word's letters

parts.note: a cue is the stick used to strike the ball in snooker

explanation.surface: Advice on where a player left their snooker gear.
explanation.definitionFit: A clue is a hint, the same sense as a tip given to help someone.

clue.text: Army officer's weapon prepared around range when training

parts.note: a lance is a long spear carried by a mounted soldier

indicators.note: around says the first word's letters go about the others

parts.note: set means ready or prepared, as in all set

indicators.note: training here means working at, so the letters of range are reshaped

explanation.surface: A soldier's weapon is readied around the firing range during drill.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's after officer stands for 'is', linking definition to wordplay; 'range' looks like a firing range but is only letters to rearrange.
explanation.definitionFit: A lance sergeant was a British Army rank, a corporal acting as a sergeant.

clue.text: Denounce former partner, City judge

parts.note: an ex is a former husband, wife or partner
EC is the postcode of the City of London, the capital's financial district
to rate something is to judge its worth

explanation.surface: A former spouse condemns a judge in the City of London.
explanation.definitionFit: To execrate is to curse or condemn something vehemently.

clue.text: In South American port, notice transistor maybe

indicators.note: In says the notice is placed inside the port's name

parts.note: Rio de Janeiro, the Brazilian port, is commonly called Rio
an ad is a notice advertising something

explanation.surface: An advertisement for a transistor set seen in a Brazilian port.
explanation.definitionFit: A transistor was the old name for a small portable radio set, so it is an example.

clue.text: Love affair, with fabulous bird enthralling chap, European

indicators.note: to enthral is to hold captive, so the bird holds the chap within it

parts.note: the roc is a giant bird of legend, from the Arabian Nights
a chap is a man

explanation.surface: A love affair where a legendary bird captivates a European man.
explanation.definitionFit: A romance is a love affair, especially a short or idealised one.

clue.text: Noble Tim, a fencing freak

indicators.note: a freak is an oddity, so the letters are set out in a strange new order

explanation.surface: An aristocratic Tim who is a fencing fanatic.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Noble' sounds like a title for Tim, but it is the adjective meaning grand or splendid.
explanation.definitionFit: Magnificent means impressively grand, and noble can mean imposing in appearance, a near-synonym.

clue.text: Part of day, we are shortening formal attire

parts.note: the evening is the part of the day after the afternoon

indicators.note: shortening cuts the end off, losing the final letter of the phrase

parts.note: the two words as written, run together

explanation.surface: A guest explaining that evenings are when they cut back on dressing up.
explanation.definitionFit: Evening wear is the smart clothing worn to formal occasions at night, such as dinner jackets and gowns.

clue.text: Introduced quiet official before pilot departs

parts.note: p is the musical notation for piano, quietly
a ref is a referee, a sports official
an ace is an expert pilot, especially a fighter pilot
d is the timetable abbreviation for departs

explanation.surface: A quiet referee is introduced before the pilot leaves.
explanation.definitionFit: To have prefaced a talk or book is to have introduced it with opening remarks.

clue.text: Type of film Mick regularly recorded in space

indicators.note: recorded in says the letters are written into the space

parts.note: room means space, as in room to move

indicators.note: regularly picks every other letter of the name, starting from the first

explanation.surface: Mick films something in a room on a regular basis.
explanation.definitionFit: A romcom is a romantic comedy, a genre of film.

clue.text: Mum is reversing fast

indicators.note: reversing says the word is is read backwards

parts.note: Lent is the Christian period of fasting before Easter

explanation.surface: Mother is driving backwards quickly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mum' looks like a mother but is the adjective meaning saying nothing, as in keep mum.
explanation.definitionFit: To be mum is to be quiet and say nothing, a synonym of saying nothing at all.

clue.text: Dicky tucks into part of fish substitute

indicators.note: tucks into places the first piece inside the fish part

parts.note: a fin is a part of a fish
dicky is informal British for weak or unwell, as in a dicky heart

explanation.surface: Someone called Dicky eats part of a fish as a stand-in.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dicky' looks like a name; it is British slang for poorly, and 'tucks into' looks like eating.
explanation.definitionFit: A fill-in is a person or thing serving temporarily in place of another, a stand-in.

clue.text: Pop's one to vocalise, daydreaming

parts.note: pop is fizzy drink, and Fanta is a brand of it; with the apostrophe s
I is the Roman numeral for one
to sing is to vocalise

explanation.surface: A father who wants to be a singer is lost in a daydream.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pop' suggests a father or pop music; here it is fizzy drink, and Fanta is a brand of orange soda.
explanation.definitionFit: Fantasising means imagining pleasant unlikely things, a synonym of the present participle for idle reverie.

clue.text: Spot on side of dice: pip

indicators.note: in a down clue on means placed above, so the first piece comes before

parts.note: to spot is to see

indicators.note: side of takes the edge letter of the word, its first

explanation.surface: A spot on a die's face is called a pip.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface uses pip in its sense of a dot on a die; the answer takes its fruit sense.
explanation.definitionFit: A pip is the small seed of a fruit such as an apple or orange.

clue.text: Fortress constructed at the front with elaborate detail

indicators.note: at the front takes just the opening letter of the word before it
elaborate means worked up and complicated, so the letters of detail are rearranged

explanation.surface: A fortress built with ornate decoration on its facade.
explanation.definitionFit: A citadel is a fortress, typically one guarding or overlooking a city.

clue.text: Destroy period staircase heartlessly

parts.note: an era is a period of history

indicators.note: without its heart, only the first and last letters of the word remain

explanation.surface: Someone callously demolishing a staircase from a historic period.
explanation.definitionFit: To erase is to wipe out or obliterate, so to destroy all trace of something.

clue.text: Daughter perhaps painting English river

parts.note: painting is an example of art, hence perhaps

explanation.surface: A daughter who may be painting by an English river.
explanation.definitionFit: The Dart is a river in Devon, in south-west England, flowing out at Dartmouth.

clue.text: Condition inside half of ground not declared

indicators.note: inside puts the condition within the other letters
half of takes the latter three of the word's six letters

parts.note: a state is a condition, as in a state of repair

explanation.surface: A condition of the land that was never declared.
explanation.definitionFit: Something unstated has not been said or expressed, so it is undeclared.
